title: Function That Always Says Hello
statement:
Write createHelloWorld(). It takes no arguments and returns a function. That returned function accepts any number of arguments of any type, ignores all of them, and always returns the string "Hello World".

The test harness can only pass plain data, not call the function you return. So the tested entry point is helloForEachCall(calls): build the greeter once with createHelloWorld(), call it once per entry of calls (each entry is the argument list for that call, spread into the call), and return the results in order.

examples.why: Numbers, strings, null, arrays and objects are all ignored. The greeting never changes.
The greeter is created but never called, so there are no results.

constraints: Each argument list has 0 to 10 entries of any JSON type
hints: A function in JavaScript is a value. createHelloWorld can return one just like it returns a number.
Rest parameters, (...args) => ..., let a function accept any number of arguments. It does not have to use them.
Return an arrow function that ignores its arguments and returns the fixed string.

explain.intuition:
This is a warm-up about functions as values. createHelloWorld is a factory: calling it does not greet anyone, it hands you a new function that will greet when called. The same shape appears all over frontend code: event handler factories, useCallback, middleware, and debounce wrappers all return functions.

The returned function ignores whatever is passed. Declaring ...args documents that any arguments are accepted, and JavaScript does not complain about extra arguments even without it.
steps: Define createHelloWorld so that it returns (...args) => "Hello World".
In helloForEachCall, call createHelloWorld() once to get the greeter.
Map each argument list in calls to greeter(...args) and return the results.
pitfalls: Returning the string from createHelloWorld itself instead of returning a function that returns the string.
Echoing an argument back, for example returning args[0] when it happens to be a string.
In Python, forgetting *args in the inner function, so calls with arguments raise a TypeError.

solutions.title: Return an arrow function
solutions.idea: The factory returns a function that ignores its arguments and returns the fixed string.

followups: Change the factory to take a name and return a function that greets that name. What does the inner function remember, and where is it stored?
Write once(fn): it returns a function that calls fn the first time and returns the same result on every later call.
